head.title: Carte figurative des pertes successives en hommes de l'armée française dans la campagne de Russie 1812–1813, comparée à celle d'Annibal durant la 2ᵉᵐᵉ guerre punique
head.subtitle: BnF, Ge Don 4182 · lithograph · 62 × 54 cm · Paris, 20 novembre 1869 · Minard was 88, and died ten months later during the siege of Paris

notes.words: the sheet is drawn at its own aspect — 2.258 px per millimetre of Minard's paper, so every band width on screen is a real millimetre count
THE PLATE STATES ITS OWN CONSTRUCTION RULE.  THIS SKETCH CHECKS IT — AND THEN CHECKS ITSELF WITH THE SAME MEASUREMENT.

titles.words: Carte Figurative des pertes successives en hommes de l'armée qu'Annibal conduisit d'Espagne
en Italie en traversant les Gaules (selon Polybe).
Dressée par M. Minard, Inspecteur Général des Ponts et Chaussées en retraite.

legend.heading: Légende.
lines: Les nombres d'hommes restés à Annibal sont représentés
par la largeur des zônes colorées à raison d'un millimètre
pour dix mille hommes, ils sont de plus écrits en travers des zônes.
Il n'y a pas d'opinion arrêtée sur le point où Annibal a
traversé les Alpes, j'ai adopté celle de Larosa sans prétendre la justifier.

NEGATIVE RESULT — and it is the more useful half: the famous 12,000→14,000 anomaly is NOT
measurable in the ink. At the floor both readings are 5.4 px. The prettier finding does not exist.

cards.title: THE MAP IS A REAL MAP

notes.words: median 5.35 km on an 871 km span — 0.6%. The received account is wrong.
residual is within 1.8× of what the 0.1° digitisation grid alone produces

TOTAL 934.2 km real → 944.6 km on Minard, ratio 1.011 — one leg squeezed to 59%, the next stretched to 153%, the total kept right,
exactly where Wizma, Chjat and Mojaisk crowd into 130 px of lettering.  That the room was for the labels is an INFERENCE.
°C = °R × 5/4      °F = °R × 9/4 + 32      (exact — Réaumur puts 80 degrees between ice and steam)

−30 °R = −37.50 °C = −35.50 °F.  The plate's title says degrés du
thermomètre de Réaumur in display capitals, and reproductions still
relabel the axis Celsius while keeping his numbers.

Hannibal 218 BC    96,000 → 26,000    survived 27.08%
Napoleon 1812     422,000 → 10,000    survived  2.37%
This is why he printed them together.

projection.t: THE PROJECTION — re-measured here, and one finding is new
Napoleon panel, tan centreline, 8 stations east of Polotzk:
d = 280.3 px/deg lat,  d/b = 2.142,  R² 0.866, rms 34 px
Hannibal panel, same fit, 11 stations, BnF sheet:
→ THE TWO PANELS DO NOT SHARE A PROJECTION. The top one is a STRIP,
not a map: latitude explains an eighth of the band's height. So the
received "Minard sacrificed geography" is wrong about the panel every-
one quotes and right about the panel nobody looks at.

own.head.t: THE SKETCH'S OWN GEOMETRY — the same auditor, turned round

own.outline.t: so the two disagree, and the outline is what they disagree about. A min-chord

own.seams.t: goes in and out along every interior seam: no area, no ink, and fatal to a chord.
⇒ A WIDTH AUDIT IS ONLY AS GOOD AS THE OUTLINE IT CROSSES. Reported, not fudged.

own.brush.t: Both zones are one brush::Ribbon on the width Profile seam, bevelled at the
joins — the chord across the outside of the turn, and the inside fills as a union.

own.corner.t: → the corner this sheet is hardest on is Wilna's: 130 px of band turning on an
86 px leg, where the union of the steps is thicker than the law and the
outline folds over itself. It draws solid.
